record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: For a self-referential Liar Paradox sentence treated as a temporal oscillator that alternates between truth values through natural time, what determines the oscillator’s rate of time, and how is that rate related to the frame rate of the cognitive system observing and calculating the sentence’s truth value?

evidence.quote:
Grim started with the basic Liar Paradox (“This
sentence is false”) and pointed out that it is a paradox only if one insists on a single constant (i.e., time-
less) truth value. If one places this self-referential sentence in what we call natural time, unwinding the
circle into a helix as in figure 2, then it can be seen to encode a simple oscillator that bounces between
TRUE and FALSE through time.

One interesting question here is the rate of time: how fast does the Liar Paradox oscillate? It is
relative, to the frame rate of whatever cognitive system is observing it and calculating the truth value.
This is another kind of time that is set by the cognitive system and its interaction with the world.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Liar sentence L := "L is false." Rather than assigning L a single, time-independent truth value, model L as a discrete-time dynamical system whose state at step n is a truth value v_n ∈ {TRUE, FALSE}, updated by the involution v_{n+1} = ¬v_n, so that the trajectory unwinds the self-referential circle into a helix oscillating between TRUE and FALSE. Suppose an external cognitive observer evaluates L by repeatedly substituting the current truth value into the sentence at a discrete "frame rate" f_obs (evaluations per unit external time), producing one update of v_n per frame.

(a) Determine what intrinsic quantity, if any, sets the oscillator's own rate of time (its period or frequency in some natural time parameter), independent of any observer.

(b) Derive the precise relationship between the oscillation frequency f_L observed for L and the observer's frame rate f_obs, including the period in units of the observer's frames and any aliasing or relativistic-style dependence on f_obs.

(c) State conditions under which the oscillation rate is well-defined as an invariant of the sentence alone, versus conditions under which it is only definable relative to the observing cognitive system.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conceptual open problem about modeling self-reference as temporal oscillation; no formal mathematical resolution determining the intrinsic vs. observer-relative rate of a Liar-paradox oscillator appears in the literature. Related work by Grim and others on the dynamics of paradox treats truth-value oscillation qualitatively rather than fixing a canonical rate, leaving the precise rate-vs.-frame-rate relationship unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Self-Reference and Chaos in Fuzzy Logic (Grim)
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the Liar and related self-referential sentences as dynamical systems exhibiting oscillation and chaos, but does not fix an absolute oscillation rate independent of the evaluating system.
status_evidence.claim: Prior dynamical-systems treatments of the Liar describe oscillation qualitatively without determining an intrinsic rate.
